dt:tractionlife-2022-st-mt-review.title: 2022 Honda Civic Sport Touring Hatchback Review (Manual)

candidates.locator: Powertrain section, paragraph beginning 'A new 6-speed manual transmission'
candidates.evidence: A new 6-speed manual transmission is available in all grades. The transmission has been revised for an even sportier feel with improved shift rigidity and shorter shift throws. A new dual-mass flywheel helps reduce noise and vibration transmitted through the drivetrain.

applicability.notes: 2022 launch release; 6MT carried over unchanged 2022-2024 per identical US ratio tables

candidates.notes: Contrast: the 11th-gen Si uses a single-mass flywheel (different part 22100-65P-003); not applicable here.

drivetrain.flywheel_part_number.description: OEM flywheel part number (1.5T Sport Touring 6MT)

candidates.evidence: 2024 Honda Civic Flywheel Part Number: 22100-5CD-018 … Replaces : 22100-5CD-008 … Fits the following 2024 Honda Civic Submodels: 5 Door 1.5T Sport Touring | 6MT
candidates.notes: Distinct from the Si (22100-65P-003), Type R (22100-65W-003) and 2.0L Sport 6MT (22100-65M-003) flywheels. MSRP $2458.10 vs $635.23 for the Si single-mass part is consistent with a dual-mass unit. Listed 'Item Weight: 34.60 Pounds' with box dimensions 15.5 x 15.2 x 6.1 in is a shipping weight, NOT a flywheel mass.

drivetrain.flywheel_shipping_weight.description: Listed item (shipping) weight of OEM flywheel 22100-5CD-018 — upper bound on flywheel mass only

candidates.evidence: Item Weight : 34.60 Pounds Item Dimensions : 15.5 x 15.2 x 6.1 inches
candidates.notes: Retailer shipping data (box dims listed); includes packaging. Use only as an upper bound for flywheel mass.

candidates.evidence: 2024 Honda Civic Differential Complete Part Number: 41100-57A-000 … Other Name : Differential Case … Fits the following 2024 Honda Civic Submodels: 5 Door 1.5T Sport Touring, 5 Door 2.0L Sport | 6MT
candidates.notes: Same listing shows the Si gets 'Differential Assembly, Helical Limited Slip' 41200-5CD-003 and the Type R 'LSD, ASSY- HELICAL' 41200-R3P-003; the Sport Touring 6MT part is not an LSD. No Honda spec sheet lists an LSD for the hatchback. Brake-based yaw control is separate: see drivetrain.agile_handling_assist.

drivetrain.agile_handling_assist.description: Agile Handling Assist (brake-based yaw-moment control) fitted

candidates.notes: Listed as a chassis feature, not as a differential. AHA applies light individual-wheel braking to aid turn-in (yaw moment); Honda does not describe it as a limited-slip substitute and no evidence was found that it acts as a brake-based LSD on power. Do not model as an LSD.

candidates.how_to_measure: Stop the real car in neutral with the clutch released, engine warm: note whether the engine shuts off and the idle-stop lamp lights; or read the owner's manual 'Auto Idle Stop' section for the MT.
candidates.notes: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE: 2024 Canadian and US spec tables mark Idle-stop for every trim column (the ST column includes the 6MT), but the 2022 Honda Canada launch release says 'a new standard idle-stop system (CVT only)' (dt:hondanews-ca-2022-hatch-debut, Powertrain paragraph on the 2.0L LX). Owner's manual not checked. Not decisive; treated as unknown-leaning-yes.

candidates.value: 6MT revised for improved shift rigidity and shorter shift throws
candidates.evidence: The transmission has been revised for an even sportier feel with improved shift rigidity and shorter shift throws.
candidates.as_printed: improved shift rigidity and shorter shift throws

applicability.notes: 2022 launch release; 6MT carried over unchanged 2022-2024 per identical US ratio tables

candidates.notes: 'cable-operated' is not stated by this source; hondapartsnow lists 'Shift Cable' among related 2024 Civic parts (lead only).

candidates.value: single dry plate, rigid (unsprung) hub disc; torsional damping in the dual-mass flywheel
candidates.evidence: Also blown away the oem clutch disc has no springs on it at all. All of the dampening for the oem system comes from the dual mass flywheel
candidates.as_printed: oem clutch disc has no springs
candidates.notes: 'single dry plate' is the conventional FWD manual layout, not stated by the source. Rigid disc is consistent with a DMF (dt flywheel_type, class A).

candidates.value: hydraulic (master cylinder, line with in-line damper)
candidates.evidence: even when I adjusted the stroke of the clutch master cylinder to the longest … I even deleted on the stupid in-line clutch damper and replaced the rubber oem clutch line
candidates.as_printed: clutch master cylinder … in-line clutch damper … oem clutch line
candidates.notes: Owner posts; parts catalog clutch-hydraulics diagram not opened (lead).

drivetrain.clutch_torque_capacity.description: Clutch static torque capacity (or clamp load)

candidates.how_to_measure: Not measurable without a test rig; derive from pressure-plate clamp load (published by aftermarket makers for the OEM unit), facing diameters and friction coefficient (~0.27-0.32 organic).
candidates.notes: An owner post says the OEM pressure plate is 'approximately 500kg, I believe' — hearsay, not recorded as a value. Stock car does not slip at 177 lb-ft (240 N*m), so capacity > 240 N*m.
searches: hondapartsnow 2024 Civic flywheel/differential listings (no clutch dimensions)
WebSearch: 11th gen Civic 1.5T 6MT clutch kit OEM disc diameter (Exedy/ACT/Clutch Masters)

candidates.how_to_measure: Remove the DMF and clutch cover; bifilar/trifilar pendulum or measure mass and outer/inner radii of each disc; or estimate from free-revving rpm decay logged at clutch-in with known engine friction.
candidates.notes: DMF primary and secondary inertias differ; for a sim a lumped value is used. Shipping weight 34.6 lb (incl. box) is an upper bound on mass.
searches: hondapartsnow flywheel listing (only a shipping weight)

drivetrain.driveline_inertia.description: Driveline rotating inertia downstream of clutch (gearbox, diff, halfshafts), referred to wheels

candidates.how_to_measure: Coast-down / free-roll test with the car on a lift (wheel spin-down in neutral vs in gear), or CAD of the gearset; small relative to wheel+tyre inertia.
searches: no published data for this gearbox

drivetrain.rev_hang_qualitative.description: Rev hang on throttle lift / clutch-in (qualitative)

candidates.evidence: There’s also some rev hang, so you’ll need to be patient before dumping the clutch on your next gear.
candidates.notes: Qualitative only; duration and rpm amount unknown (see drivetrain.rev_hang_duration).

drivetrain.rev_hang_duration.description: Rev hang: time for rpm to fall after clutch-in at high rpm, and rpm held

candidates.how_to_measure: OBD-II log (>=10 Hz rpm, throttle, clutch switch if available) of 3000->idle and 6000->idle drops with clutch in after a full-throttle pull; and rpm trace during 1-2 and 2-3 upshifts. Report time to drop 1000 rpm and any plateau.
candidates.notes: Do not model a specific hang until logged.
searches: WebSearch: 2022 Civic hatchback Sport Touring manual rpm/rev hang review

drivetrain.shift_time.description: Gear-change time (clutch open to closed) for a brisk human shift

candidates.how_to_measure: Datalog clutch switch / rpm during brisk shifts; or time from video with on-screen tach.
candidates.notes: Basis: typical brisk manual shifts in road tests take ~0.2-0.5 s; reviewer-reported rev hang argues against shorter values. Not a measurement of this car.

candidates.how_to_measure: Check owner's manual for 'Rev Match Control' or test: downshift with clutch in and watch for an automatic blip.
candidates.notes: Absence from all Honda spec tables suggests not fitted (unlike Si/Type R), but absence is not recorded as evidence.
